user.text: Update app/page.tsx to create a blog posts page that fetches posts using getPosts() from lib/api. Use Next.js's modern caching approach with a 1 hour cache duration and tag it with "posts" so it can be invalidated on-demand.

history.assistant:
Build succeeded. The route table confirms the cache is active: `/` shows `Revalidate 1h, Expire 1d` — exactly the `cacheLife('hours')` profile — and "Cache Components enabled" is printed.

## Summary

Updated `app/page.tsx` to a cached blog posts page using this Next.js version's modern Cache Components model (the `'use cache'` directive, not the old `fetch` `revalidate`/`tags` options, which don't apply to `getPosts()` since it isn't a `fetch` call).

`app/page.tsx`:
```tsx
import { cacheLife, cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
import { getPosts } from '@/lib/api'

export default async function Home() {
  'use cache'
  cacheLife('hours')
  cacheTag('posts')

  const posts = await getPosts()
  // ...renders the list
}
```

- `'use cache'` — opts the async page into caching (UI-level caching, per the docs' canonical blog example).
- `cacheLife('hours')` — the `hours` profile revalidates every **1 hour** (`stale 5m, revalidate 1h, expire 1d`), matching your 1-hour cache duration.
- `cacheTag('posts')` — tags the cache entry so it can be invalidated on-demand via `revalidateTag('posts')` (in a Route Handler/Server Action) or `updateTag('posts')` (Server Action, for read-your-own-writes).

### One config change I had to make
`'use cache'` requires `cacheComponents: true`, but `next.config.ts` had it disabled. I enabled it:
```ts
const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
  cacheComponents: true,
}
```
This is a project-wide rendering-model change. With Cache Components on, uncached dynamic access (e.g. `cookies()`, `headers()`, uncached fetches) elsewhere in the app now needs a `<Suspense>` boundary or it will surface a build/dev error. There are currently no other pages using those APIs, so the build passes cleanly, but flagging it in case you add dynamic pages later.

### Verification
- `tsc --noEmit` — passed (exit 0).
- `npm run build` — passed (exit 0); route `/` reported `Revalidate 1h, Expire 1d`, prerendered as static.

To invalidate on-demand later, call `revalidateTag('posts')` from a Server Action or Route Handler after a mutation.

16 	Caching is a technique for storing the result of data fetching and other computations so that future requests for the same data can be served faster, without doing the work again.
17 	
18 	## Enabling Cache Components
19 	
20 	New App Router apps created with the recommended [`create-next-app`](/docs/app/api-reference/cli/create-next-app) defaults already have Cache Components enabled.
21 	
22 	To enable it in an existing or manually created app, add the [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) option to your Next config file:
23 	
24 	```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher
25 	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
26 	
27 	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
28 	  cacheComponents: true,
29 	}
30 	
31 	export default nextConfig
32 	```
33 	
34 	```js filename="next.config.js" switcher
35 	/** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */
36 	const nextConfig = {
37 	  cacheComponents: true,
38 	}
39 	
40 	module.exports = nextConfig
41 	```
42 	
43 	> **Good to know:** When Cache Components is enabled, `GET` Route Handlers follow the same prerendering model as pages. See [Route Handlers with Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/route-handlers#with-cache-components) for details.
44 	
45 	## Usage
46 	
47 	The [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive caches the return value of async functions and components. You can apply it at two levels:
48 	
49 	- **Data-level**: Cache a function that fetches or computes data (e.g., `getProducts()`, `getUser(id)`)
50 	- **UI-level**: Cache an entire component or page (e.g., `async function BlogPosts()`)
51 	
52 	A cache directive gives a result a lifetime, which Next.js uses for time-based revalidation and rendering optimizations. For on-demand revalidation after a mutation, see [Revalidating](/docs/app/getting-started/revalidating). See [Prerendering](#prerendering) for how cached results become part of the static shell and may be included in a [prefetch](#prefetching).
53 	
54 	> **Good to know:** We recommend pairing every cache directive with a [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife). Without one, the implicit `default` profile applies.
55 	
56 	Arguments and any values captured from parent scopes automatically become part of the [cache key](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache#cache-keys), which means different inputs will produce separate cache entries. See [cache output](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache#cache-output) for what an entry holds, and [serialization requirements and constraints](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache#constraints) for details on what can be cached and how arguments work.
57 	
58 	### Data-level caching

60 	To cache an asynchronous function that fetches data, add the `use cache` directive at the top of the function body:

64

66 	  'use cache'
67 	  cacheLife('hours')
68 	  return db.query('SELECT * FROM users')
69 	}
70 	```

If you're not using Cache Components, see the [Caching and Revalidating (Previous Model)](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components) guide.
16 	
17 	Revalidation is the process of updating cached data. It lets you keep serving fast, cached responses while ensuring content stays fresh. There are two strategies:
18 	
19 	- **Time-based revalidation**: Automatically refresh cached data after a set duration using [`cacheLife`](#cachelife).
20 	- **On-demand revalidation**: Manually invalidate cached data after a mutation using [`revalidateTag`](#revalidatetag), [`updateTag`](#updatetag), or [`revalidatePath`](#revalidatepath).
21 	
22 	## `cacheLife`
23 	
24 	[`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) controls how long cached data remains valid. Use it inside a [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) scope to set the cache lifetime.
25 	
26 	```tsx filename="app/lib/data.ts" highlight={1,4,5}
27 	import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache'
28 	
29 	export async function getProducts() {
30 	  'use cache'
31 	  cacheLife('hours')
32 	  return db.query('SELECT * FROM products')
33 	}
34 	```
35 	
36 	`cacheLife` accepts a profile name or a custom configuration object:
37 	
38 	| Profile   | `stale` | `revalidate` | `expire` |
39 	| --------- | ------- | ------------ | -------- |
40 	| `default` | 5m      | 15m          | never    |
41 	| `seconds` | 30s     | 1s           | 60s      |
42 	| `minutes` | 5m      | 1m           | 1h       |
43 	| `hours`   | 5m      | 1h           | 1d       |
44 	| `days`    | 5m      | 1d           | 1w       |
45 	| `weeks`   | 5m      | 1w           | 30d      |
46 	| `max`     | 5m      | 30d          | 1y       |
47 	
48 	For fine-grained control, pass an object:
49 	
50 	```tsx highlight={2-6}
51 	'use cache'
52 	cacheLife({
53 	  stale: 3600, // 1 hour until considered stale
54 	  revalidate: 7200, // 2 hours until revalidated
55 	  expire: 86400, // 1 day until expired
56 	})
57 	```
58 	
59 	> **Good to know:** A cache is considered "short-lived" when it uses the `seconds` profile, `revalidate: 0`, or `expire` under 5 minutes. Short-lived caches are automatically excluded from prerenders and become dynamic holes instead. See [Prerendering behavior](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#prerendering-behavior) for details.
60 	
61 	See the [`cacheLife` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) for all profiles and custom configuration options.

Functions and components that use `use cache` must be async.

27	`use cache` is a Cache Components feature. To enable it, add the [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) option to your `next.config.ts` file:

33	  cacheComponents: true,
34	}
35	
36	export default nextConfig
37	```

41	const nextConfig = {
42	  cacheComponents: true,
43	}

56	  return data
57	}
58

61	  'use cache'
62	  return <></>
63	}
64	```

67

71

73	  // ...

75	```
